observation.visible_scene: A close, top-down view of two hands (dark ribbed sleeves) over a square gray metallic plate on a white surface, each hand holding a short chain of glossy golden cubes. The left hand grips one segment and the right hand grips another; throughout the clip the hands press the two segments together at a single joint and rotate them, gradually forming an L-shaped assembly made of a vertical column of cubes (left hand) meeting a horizontal 2-row block (right hand) at a corner.
visible_changes: The two golden segments start nearly aligned end-to-end in the center of the frame and are brought into firm contact at one cube.
As the clip progresses the relative angle between the segments changes from roughly straight to a clear right angle, producing an L / corner shape held between the two hands.
The left segment reorients from a horizontal-ish stub into a vertical column, while the right segment stays as a horizontal block at the top of the column.
Both hands translate upward and inward, repositioning the joined assembly higher in the frame and closer to the plate's top edge.
Small continuous rotations and thumb/finger adjustments are made at the corner joint; the assembly is held steady rather than being dropped or separated.
The gray plate and the hands' framing shift size/position across frames, consistent with the assembly being moved relative to the camera (and possibly a slight camera reframing).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the two segments were fully separate before t=0 or already partly connected (the clip opens mid-manipulation).
What the final intended shape or action is after t=2.67 s (the clip ends with the L-shape still being held).
The mechanism of the joint (e.g., magnetic vs. hinged) and the total number of cubes in each segment, which are partly occluded by the fingers.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the change in the plate's apparent size/position is camera movement or the hands lifting the assembly toward the lens.
The exact cube count per segment is hard to verify because fingers occlude several cubes.
Whether the corner joint is being newly connected or merely rotated while already connected is not fully resolvable from the sampled frames.
